ca_tunnel_rock.blurb: Tunnel Rock is a set of small walls on Donner Summit, tucked directly above the Snowshed Wall. It is a quiet spot for the summit, and one of the few faces up there that look north. Most of the ten routes are trad, with a couple of sport lines and one top rope. About half are easy to moderate, roughly 5.5 to 5.8, which makes it a decent pick for newer leaders building mileage on low-angle cracks and slabs. A handful of harder lines go from 5.10 into the low 5.12s, including a slab and a few bolted routes.

ca_eppulator_vicinity.blurb: Eppulator Vicinity is a tight cluster of boulders in the Jaws Boulder Area on Mt. Woodson in San Diego County, and it is among the busiest and most concentrated problem zones on the hill. Of its ten lines, eight are boulder problems and two are short trad climbs. The problems start around V1 and run through the mid grades, with a few real tests at V7 and one at V10, while the two roped lines sit at 5.10 and 5.11. Expect short, technical climbing on a hillside with no trail signs, so bring pads and a spotter.

ca_rowell_rock.blurb: Rowell Rock is the largest boulder in a small group beside the trail in the Buttermilks outside Bishop, just downhill from the Buttermilk Stem boulder. Its ten problems are slabby and thin, with crimpy faces and several highballs, so it rewards footwork and a calm head more than raw power. The grades split into two camps: about half are V0 to V1 and easy to hop on, then a lone V4, and a hard top end from V8 to V10 that few climbers try. Bring several pads and a spotter for the taller lines.

ca_rated_x_boulder.blurb: Rated X Boulder is a single sunny block beside the trail to Summit Lake, in the Trailside Boulders near Donner Summit off I-80. It holds ten problems and has the widest range of the group, from a V0 warm-up up to V10. The middle grades are the draw, with the namesake line at V4 plus several V5 and V6 problems, and a hard top end above that. The granodiorite sits at around 7,200 feet in an alpine setting. It is a short walk from the car, which makes it easy to combine with nearby blocks.
ca_rated_x_boulder.approach: Follow the signed main trail toward Summit Lake; the boulder stands alone on the right side of the trail about three minutes from the lot.

ca_tic_tock_boulder.blurb: Tic Tock Boulder is one of the blocks in the Split Rock Area of Donner Memorial State Park, near Truckee, standing about a hundred feet west of Split Rock beside an amphitheater. It carries ten problems that lean toward the friendly side: several are V0 or V1 and make good warm-ups, a few sit at V3, and there are a couple of harder lines up to V8. At roughly 6,000 feet, it makes an easy add-on to the nearby Split Rock problems.

ca_right_wall_2.blurb: Right Wall is the face to the right of the tower on The Wedge, high on El Cajon Mountain in San Diego County. Ten routes, split evenly between sport and trad, cover a wide span from about 5.7 up to 5.13, with a cluster in the 5.10 and 5.11 range. The rock is mostly good quality, but the amount of traffic and development means rockfall from other parties is a concern, so a helmet is worth wearing. The wall takes sun for most of the day, with some relief late in the afternoon, so summer outings get hot and need plenty of water. It is a long hike in from the road.

ca_shipwreck_wall.blurb: Shipwreck Wall is a bolted sandstone face on the ocean side of Sentinel Rock in Salt Point State Park, north of Jenner. All ten routes are sport climbs, and the wall is a place for strong climbers: two sit around 5.10, two around 5.11, and six are 5.12. The rock is mostly solid and vertical, though it can turn crumbly near the tops of lines. You reach the base by walking along the beach and over big rocks. The wall catches afternoon sun, and the sea-cliff setting makes sunset sessions memorable.
